newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila stocks seen rising again after pause.
newsitem.headline: Manila stocks seen rising again after pause.

text.p: The Philippine stock market index surged to a record close for the second straight day on Friday and analysts said the run into unchartered territory would resume again next week after a short break.
"The market has achieved what we thought it would be doing this week which is to hold the 3,400 index level," said Helen Alvarez, research head at All Asia Securities.
The main index closed up 29.15 points, or 0.86 percent, to 3,421.91 points on Friday, after vaulting through major resistance at 3,400.
The index finished the week up 89.38 points, or 2.68 percent, from the previous Friday's close of 3,332.53.
President Fidel Ramos remarked on the market's strength during a press conference on Friday afternoon, saying the rise was a sign of investor confidence in the Philippines.

Stock market traders, analysts and government finance officials said the bullishness was spurred by the country's strong economic performance along with the release of a number of positive company earnings reports, and these factors would continue to boost the market in the longer-term.
However, analysts said mild profit-taking, the Chinese Lunar New Year holidays and a meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve board next week were likely to prompt a short correction.

"...we will see a shallow correction next week. The momentum is too strong to have a long-lasting correction. After that, our next target will be 3,600," said Noel Reyes, research head at Anscor Hagedorn Securities Inc.
BPI Capital Corp analyst Spencer Yap said the celebration of the Chinese New Year on February 7 might dampen next week's trading.
"Historically, we see Chinese investors taking a break and selling ahead of the New Year," said Manuel Goseco, Dharmala Securities Phils Inc analyst.

"There's also the Federal Reserve's meeting next week and despite expectations that interest rates will be unchanged, some investors may not take the chance and decide to take profits," said Cilette Liboro, research head at Citisecurities Inc.
Felix Barrientos, dealer at ING Barings said the performance of the market would also depend on the U.S. stock market's movements.
BPI's Yap said that after slight profit-taking next week, the market would resume its gains as more positive company earnings results are expected.
Blue-chips that have yet to release their 1996 financial statements are Manila Electric Co (Meralco), Ayala Corp, Ayala Land Inc and the Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co (PLDT).

The announcement of January inflation figures next week is also expected to lift market sentiment. The National Statistics Office (NSO) has said it will announce the inflation rate for January on February 5.

"Overall, the bullishness of the market will stay and with inflation figures expected to be lower than last year's level and that of December's, we see the equities market becoming more attractive," said Alvarez at All Asia.
Alvarez added she expected January inflation to be at 5.05 percent year-on-year against 5.1 percent in December and 11.2 percent in January last year.
